title: The Guardian: Build it yourself at the UK's first bamboo bike workshop (2012)
body_html:
In November 2012, just two months after the Bamboo Bicycle Club launched, the Guardian's Bike Blog ran a feature on our monthly workshops in Hackney Wick, east London. Written by James Stewart, it was the first national press coverage we ever received.

Stewart spent a Saturday morning with builders mitring bamboo, setting tubes in jigs and wrapping joints — and summed the day up in a line we still love:

"Woodwork class was never like this."

At the time, a place on the course was £389 and included a computer-designed custom frame and a weekend of building. The club was founded by James Marr and Ian McMillan, who had spent years developing the bamboo frame-building process before opening it up to the public.

Read the original article on The Guardian: Build it yourself at the UK's first bamboo bike workshop — The Guardian, 16 November 2012

---

*Editor's note: this page previously credited the coverage to the Hindustan Times. That attribution was incorrect — the article was written by James Stewart for The Guardian Bike Blog (16 November 2012). The text, quotes and "woodwork class" line are the Guardian's. This page now points to the genuine Guardian source; the canonical post for this coverage is the Guardian post linked in the front matter.*
